hints.title: Translate equal areas into one integral
hints.body: Write the quadratic as k(x−2)(x−q), where k>0. Between 0 and 2 it is positive; between 2 and q it is negative.
hints.recap: Equal geometric areas cancel in a signed integral.
hints.pitfall: Adding the two positive areas is not the same as integrating through both regions.
hints.pause: What is the integral from 0 to q?

recall.reminder: A definite integral subtracts regions below the axis; geometric area adds their magnitudes.

hints.title: Use the roots before expanding
hints.body: Equal areas give ∫0qk(x−2)(x−q)dx = 0. Divide by the nonzero k and expand (x−2)(x−q)=x2−(q+2)x+2q.
hints.pitfall: There is no need to recover the exact height of the parabola.
hints.pause: Integrate with q treated as a constant.

recall.reminder: Integrate each power of x and subtract the lower-limit value.

hints.title: Factor the parameter equation
hints.body: Substitute the upper limit into your antiderivative, keeping the parameter in every term. Collect equal powers before factorising the resulting equation.
hints.recap: Use the location of the second root to reject the zero factor.
hints.pitfall: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is incompatible with the pictured order <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Solve the factored equation and check every candidate against the stated position of the second root.

recall.reminder: After factoring, test each algebraic candidate against the original restrictions.

solution:
The graph has equation y=k(x−2)(x−q), k>0 and q>2. Equal areas R and S mean that their signed contributions cancel, so ∫0qk(x−2)(x−q)dx = 0.

After cancelling k, integration gives [x33−(q+2)x22+2qx]0q = q2−q36=q2(1−q6)=0. Since q>2, q=6.

Answer E: 6.
